## 固定收益市場主線

美國消費者信心優於預期，科技股再度走高，美債則小幅下跌；市場原已傾向認為聯準會將先暫停升息、之後再度緊縮。2年期殖利率上升2.1個基點至4.7369%，10年期僅升0.83個基點至4.9967%。長天期表現再次優於短端，殖利率曲線延續趨平，尚未扭轉近期公債回升走勢。

當日更重要的融資進展來自人工智慧。銀行正準備在明年初，透過投資等級債市場為博通晶片融資方案中最高約$210億進行再融資。擬議發債以出租予Anthropic的設備及博通明訂的殘值承諾為支持，讓債權人更清楚掌握潛在供給規模及保障。Meta另已完成普通股與特別股出售，顯示資金供應仍充裕，帶動半導體股上漲3.60%；投資人同時仍仔細區分借款人及融資結構。

聯準會決策前，油價下跌稍微舒緩壓力，布蘭特原油下跌1.61%至每桶$113.95。不過，新的通膨研究顯示壓力不只來自能源：惠譽發現，美國9月CPI組成項目中，46%的年漲幅超過3%。法國消費者信心降至13年低點，也使法債吐回部分評等疑慮緩解所帶來的漲幅。美國公債當日波動不大，企業融資條件與主權風險分布卻有重要變化。

## 信心回升，美債殖利率曲線趨平

週二美債跌幅有限，賣壓集中於對近期政策決定較敏感的年期。5年期殖利率上升1.79個基點至4.8441%，30年期上升0.75個基點至5.3103%；2年與10年期利差收窄1.27個基點至25.98個基點，2年與30年期利差收窄1.35個基點至57.34個基點。家庭信心大幅優於預期，伴隨短端表現落後，但長期殖利率並未全面重新定價。

拉長比較期間，長天期公債仍較強。10年期殖利率較一週前低11.18個基點，較一個月前低16.63個基點；2年期分別下降3.92與11.71個基點。30年期週降10.95個基點、月降18.37個基點，週二只回吐其中一小部分。

10年期殖利率的小幅上升，同時來自實質殖利率及通膨補償：TIPS實質殖利率上升0.37個基點至2.6416%，損益兩平通膨率上升0.46個基點至2.3551%。過去一週，實質殖利率下降10.87個基點，損益兩平通膨率僅降0.31個基點；過去一個月，前者下降18.24個基點，後者反而上升1.61個基點。名目美債持續獲得支撐，主因仍是實質殖利率下降，而非預期通膨全面回落。

美國經濟諮商理事會10月消費者信心指數由修正後的84.2升至91.7，明顯高於市場共識81。彭博指出，這是四個月來首次回升，反映民眾對勞動市場與企業情勢轉趨樂觀，數值也高於其經濟學家調查中的所有預測。在聯準會會議前夕，家庭部門釋出的訊號因而明顯轉強。

企業投資數據則未全面走強。9月耐久財訂單成長1.8%，高於預期1.5%，亦優於8月修正後的0.1%。排除運輸後成長0.5%，雖較前月0.3%加快，仍低於預期0.6%；非國防且排除飛機的訂單也成長0.5%，不及預期0.7%，且較前月1.6%放緩。排除國防的訂單則由修正後的0.3%升至2.2%。整體訂單加速，但非國防、排除飛機類別的增幅較為溫和。

ADP每週就業增加16,800人，前期修正為17,500人。區域企業調查好壞參半，服務業大致轉強。里奇蒙聯準銀行10月製造業指數維持負2，未達預期的零，但出貨指數由負5改善至零，服務業營收指數由零升至2。達拉斯聯準銀行服務業指數由負1.8升至4.0，服務業營收指數由負0.9升至4.4。各地服務業活動有所改善，里奇蒙製造業整體指數則仍偏弱。

房市持續受融資成本限制。9月新屋銷售月減0.6%，年率由修正後68萬戶降至67.6萬戶，前月增幅則修正為5.1%。銷售量高於經濟行事曆共識65萬戶，也高於彭博另一項經濟學家調查的65.1萬戶。成交價中位數年減3.9%至$40萬400，為2026年前九個月中第七次年減。Nationwide經濟學家Daniel Vielhaber認為，銷售得以維持，主要靠建商降價及房貸優惠，而非基礎需求強勁。

區域表現也反映需求受限。最大市場南部的銷售下降6.6%至年率41.3萬戶，中西部亦下滑，抵銷西部與東北部的增幅。待售新屋較一年前減少2.3%至47.6萬戶，相當於8.4個月銷售量；供給月數雖為今年最低，仍遠高於疫情前。月度銷售估計的不確定性也很大，政府公布的90%信賴區間介於下跌14.4%與上升13.2%。

其他房市數據呈現當前融資壓力與落後房價指標的差異。9月建築許可終值月減0.4%至139.8萬戶，市場原估月減0.2%、140萬戶。8月標普／凱斯席勒房價年增率由2.5%加快至2.7%，高於預期2.5%，月變動卻由持平轉為下跌0.4%。另一項名為房價指數的數據月增0.3%，高於市場共識及修正後前值的0.2%，但年增率由修正後2.5%放緩至2.4%。

亞特蘭大聯準銀行GDPNow模型對第三季成長率的估計由3.5%下修至3.4%。截至10月24日當週，Redbook零售銷售年增率由9%升至9.3%，使部分家庭部門指標仍比房市強勁。美國財政部5年期公債標售得標殖利率為4.845%，前次為5.033%。

通膨的廣泛程度，是油價下跌之外不可忽略的另一項訊號。惠譽最新跨國評估指出，美國9月CPI組成項目中，年漲幅超過3%的占46%，為2018至2019年平均23%的兩倍；歐元區、日本與英國分別為36%、41%與42%。惠譽的Olu Sonola表示，在最近這波整體通膨加速之前，美國漲價範圍已開始擴大，意味即使能源降溫，更廣泛的價格壓力仍可能延後通膨回歸目標。

交易員評估區域外交及以色列選舉之際，布蘭特原油下跌，WTI也跌1.85%至$99.88。伊朗重申，和平談判的前提是美國終止海上封鎖及制裁，華府則要求核議題讓步。即使當日下跌，布蘭特仍較一個月前高16.94%。股市對情緒改善的反應更明顯：標普500上漲0.60%至7,722.60，那斯達克100上漲1.29%；美元指數上升0.40%至102.365。高收益債基金HYG報酬約0.52%，投資等級債基金LQD約0.27%。

部位變化使下一次聯準會溝通更為關鍵。摩根大通截至10月26日當週的調查顯示，單純做多部位增加6個百分點，中性部位減少4個百分點、空頭減少2個百分點，淨多部位升至9月8日以來最高。花旗的David Bieber形容，市場結構上仍偏空，但戰術上正轉向做多美債與歐洲債券。彭博週二報導的交換合約定價顯示，10月升息機率約8%，12月升息機率超過90%；若聯準會意外偏鷹，近期累積的看多部位可能受到挑戰。

## AI融資帶來大規模發債需求

博通為供應Anthropic晶片安排的$630億融資，如今有了更明確的公開債市再融資方向。美國銀行、花旗及摩根士丹利協助籌組，其他銀行預計未來幾天提交承諾。知情人士向彭博表示，銀行貸款約$420億，其中最高一半可能在2027年第一季透過美國投資等級債再融資。

此架構由特殊目的公司借款購買設備，包括資料中心晶片，再出租給Anthropic，以租金償還借款。銀行出資的$420億屬優先順位擔保融資，貸款人對該公司的資產享有第一順位求償權，博通另提供殘值支持。依其申報文件，潛在責任為未償租賃金額的72.5%，減去資產出售時收回的AI機櫃價值；博通認為實際承擔此項責任的可能性很低。

這項明訂範圍的支持是融資核心，並非對整體方案提供無上限保證。未來債券年期可能約五年，存續期間內逐步償還本金，最終規模與發行時點仍取決於市況。黑石則以$90億承諾，擔任其餘融資的主要出資方。

潛在$210億公開發債，將使銀行承銷的設備融資有相當部分轉入債市，而科技業借款原已異常龐大。彭博估計，今年全球各市場AI相關借款超過$4,550億；範圍較窄的全球高評級債市場，相關籌資已逾$3,000億，約為去年的三倍。兩項總額涵蓋範圍不同，但均顯示後續交易競逐投資資金時面對的供給規模。

Meta展現的則是股票需求。公司已出售$250億普通股及$125億特別股，並表示計畫再籌措最高$600億投入AI，整體籌資目標已提高至近$980億。普通股出售獲得五倍認購，即使融資活動持續增加，也有助科技股延續反彈。

貝萊德固定收益主管Rick Rieder認為，新增供給正改善債權人可取得的報酬補償。他表示，週末花了時間研究交易，也大量參與，偏好成熟企業及可創造現金流資產所發行的擔保債務。在他看來，短天期、單A評級投資組合可賺取約7%，相較承擔較長天期美債的利率風險，具有吸引力。

既有債券也反映定價改變。Meta的2036年到期債券相對美債利差超過130個基點，4月發行時則為90個基點。彭博指數顯示，美國投資等級債殖利率為5.9%，本月稍早曾接近6.1%。考量龐大融資需求，Rieder認為近期超大規模雲端業者的定價較為合理。Citadel共同投資長Pablo Salame則提出另一面：異常龐大的資金需求，碰上不願承擔全部風險的貸款人，仍可能有人受創。

公債方面，摩根資產管理的看法與Rieder不同。該公司的Bob Michele預測，美國債券未來12個月可取得約7%至8%報酬，來自利息收益與預期價格上漲。他認為長端最有價值，聯準會12月若釋出鷹派訊息，展現對通膨與成長保持警覺，反而可能支撐長天期債券。Rieder則將10年期美債更多視為市場風向指標，而非固定收益的核心機會。週二小幅殖利率變動，尚無法決定公債利率部位與企業債收益何者較佳。

BCE出售資產，則呈現AI支出如何與降槓桿爭奪資金。魁北克退休基金管理機構La Caisse同意支付C$24.5億，收購BCE無線通訊塔49.9%股權，新成立的TowerCo將擁有超過5,000個站點。BCE表示交易符合強化資產負債表及投資成長的方向；豐業銀行分析師Maher Yaghi卻預期，所得資金將再投入AI服務，而非實質降低槓桿，且在新AI投資開始貢獻之前，短期現金流影響為負。BCE目標在2027年底將淨負債降至調整後EBITDA的3.5倍，去年底約為3.8倍。

發債熱潮之下，交易結構也在變化。巴克萊策略師Zornitsa Todorova週二發布的研究發現，美國單一發行人交易最活躍的三檔債券，占該發行人債券成交量約35%，較2023年1月減少5個百分點；歐洲信用債約三年半來也出現類似下降。交易分布擴大主要發生在投資等級債，高收益債與超大規模雲端業者債券的交易仍較集中。她認為，同一發行人殖利率曲線上更多債券獲得交易，有助縮小指標券與較少交易債券的估值差距，讓投資人在供給增加時有更多年期可選。

## 法債漲勢逆轉，凸顯財政調整空間差異

法國新一波信心衝擊，暴露政治與融資壓力的經濟代價，也使法債吐回部分評等疑慮緩解後的漲幅。10年期法債相對德債利差擴大7個基點至161個基點，逆轉前一交易日收窄14個基點的部分走勢。法國國家統計及經濟研究局10月消費者信心指數下降5點至80，不僅低於預測中位數85，也低於彭博調查所有預測，創13年新低。

家庭對過往生活水準的評價降至1972年開始統計以來最差，失業預期升至疫情以來最高，個人財務展望為四年最弱，預期通膨也上升。調查雖於10月19日結束，但大多數答覆是在為期三週調查的初期、10月17日暴力事件之前取得。因此，數據已顯示家庭情況明顯惡化，卻尚未完整反映後續動亂。

融資風險同時牽涉投資人結構及銀行體系。各央行申報資料顯示，非居民持有約60%法國債務，接近十年高點；美國2025年底約為31%，英國6月底為34%。法國保險公司與銀行第二季底分別持有9.2%及10.5%。裕信銀行的Luca Cazzulani認為，外資仍有進一步賣出的空間，是市場弱點；Pimco的Konstantin Veit則表示，若例行標售需求出現問題，當局可能鼓勵國內銀行買進。

彭博行業研究估計，法國巴黎銀行、法國興業銀行與法國農業信貸銀行合計持有約€540億法國主權債，若納入保險業務則約€1,040億，其中新增的保險曝險有很大部分由保戶承擔。該機構分析師Philip Richards認為，考量攤銷後成本會計及可能的避險安排，市場對銀行直接主權風險的擔憂過度。三家銀行第二季普通股第一類資本比率分別為13.0%、13.2%及11.3%，均明顯高於監管最低要求。

更廣泛的威脅來自經濟活動走弱、貸款需求下降，以及按市價評價部位的損失。歐洲央行最新銀行放款調查顯示，歐元區銀行第三季收緊授信標準，貸款需求也減弱。銀行感知風險上升、風險容忍度下降，壓抑信貸供給；利率整體水準是需求的主要阻力，小型企業固定投資疲弱與替代融資亦有影響。銀行表示，歐洲央行縮減投資組合，對融資條件及流動性略有負面影響，但淨利息收入增加超過小額資本損失，使獲利略獲改善。

這份調查讓歐洲央行在權衡通膨與融資緊縮時，多了一項審慎理由。調查也發現，AI基礎設施貸款需求正逐步且持續成長。大多數銀行尚未針對AI貸款設定量化標準，少數則已將AI採用及相關風險納入對借款人的質化評估。整體信貸需求走弱之際，這個資本密集產業仍持續增加資金需求。

新的財政分析則質疑，美國是否能單靠分立政府，讓債市得到持久喘息。道明證券策略師Molly Brooks與Gennadiy Goldberg預測，即使選後陷入政策僵局，由於難有實質支出調整，2027會計年度赤字仍將由GDP的5.9%擴大至6.4%。Diamond Hill的Henry Song指出，公眾持有的債務已超過$32兆，年度淨利息成本逾$1兆，要穩定債務如今需要政策行動，僅不再通過新法並不足夠。

三菱日聯金融集團的George Goncalves提出另一條有條件的殖利率下降路徑：若民主黨大勝，可能加強AI監管，削弱股市與成長，並減少相關發債。三井住友銀行的Joseph Abate則認為，民主黨席次大幅增加，也可能促使共和黨推出減輕生活負擔措施及更多支出。分歧在於選舉的政策後果，並非認定國會僵局必然有利美債。

各國的財政起點也不同。彭博Chris Anstey週二比較國際貨幣基金估計指出，法國今年政府收入超過GDP的50%，美國則不到30%。法國稅負已高，進一步增收而不傷害經濟的空間有限；華府經濟上較有餘裕增稅，政治意願卻仍薄弱。對法國借款人而言，財政調整空間較窄，又逢信心下滑及利差再度擴大。

## 亞洲融資市場強弱分明

印尼主權及企業債市顯示，治理問題引發的股市衝擊已延伸至融資。10年期公債殖利率上升5個基點至7.54%，為2022年10月以來最高，印尼盾距歷史低點不到0.2%。週二政府標售需求降至三年低點，投標額31.1兆印尼盾，僅略高於30兆目標，最終發行20.7兆印尼盾。

外資動向提供另一面支撐。本月境外投資人持有的主權債增加$5.09億，顯示部分投資人回應較高殖利率。Mandiri Sekuritas研究員Handy Yunianto認為，MSCI警告的主要風險是股票資金持續外流、壓低印尼盾，而非直接影響債券指數。他估計10年期合理殖利率為7.5%至7.7%，若避險情緒與油價降溫，殖利率有下降空間。高油價也擴大補貼支出，使匯率壓力之外再添財政負擔。

Bank KB Indonesia以市場波動為由，延後週一開始行銷的美元債。擬議3年期債券預期獲惠譽BBB評級，初步定價指引約為美債加275個基點，同評級亞洲企業債約為加120個基點。國民銀行持有該行三分之二股權。野村的Nicholas Yap認為，發債困難部分來自印尼整體情緒惡化，也與該行規模小、獨立基本面弱，及趕在月底前發行有關。他預期，基本面健全的國有借款人仍能取得融資，但須提供較高的新券發行溢酬。

三星人壽的交易展現了這項區別。週二披露的細節顯示，公司週一首次發行美元次順位債，籌得$15億，票息6.875%，低於最初約7%的構想，規模創韓國壽險業紀錄，預期獲惠譽A+及穆迪A2評級。近半參與者為全球投資人，包括美國與歐洲買家。資金用於支持資本適足、股東回饋及新成長業務。惠譽Sue Kim認為，結果部分反映投資人選擇較強發行人，以及三星人壽資本對市場波動的敏感度有限。

中國公債與企業債進一步分歧。中國人民銀行透過逆回購淨投放人民幣1.01兆元，為彭博紀錄以來單日最大淨投放；5年期公債殖利率一度觸及1.34%，接近中債自2002年以來資料中的歷史收盤低點。華發境外人民幣債卻再度大幅下跌，其中一檔週二指示價格下跌創紀錄的17%，至面額約74%。華發未支付信託產品款項、要求銀行展期的消息先前已為市場所知，此次新增變化是債價進一步惡化。RatingDog的姚煜仍預期地方政府大力支持，彭博行業研究Andrew Chan則強調，相較中央國企，地方支持開發商得到的再融資支援較弱。

日本出現兩項不同的通膨加速訊號。9月企業服務價格年增3.7%，高於修正後前值3.5%；海運成本大增97.7%，為1986年有資料以來最大升幅。日本央行另一項排除生鮮食品及特殊因素的消費者物價指標，年增率由2.6%升至3.2%，創三年最高。特殊因素調整包括汽油及公用事業補貼，因此有別於政府公布的排除生鮮食品消費者物價指數。兩項數據均強化了9月政策利率升至1.25%後，持續推動正常化的理由。

殖利率走高也改變壽險資產配置。十大日本壽險公司下半年計畫顯示，業者普遍以高殖利率證券替換低收益債券，即使到期償還使整體國內持債持平或下降，仍持續換券。日本生命預期，在進行此類調整之際持債將減少，但認為當前利率具吸引力；其他業者則由匯率避險後的外債轉向國內債券。岡三證券長谷川直也預期，按單利殖利率計，10年期日債若達約3%、30年期若達約4%，需求將增強。

韓國則提出另一項緩衝。預算部長朴洪根表示，若殖利率急升或市場惡化，規劃中的未來應對基金可用於進一步減少發債。現行計畫將明年發債減少12.5兆韓元，淨發行96.3兆韓元，總發行約223兆韓元。基金明年預計收入162.3兆韓元，扣除政策支出及減少發債用途後，約三分之二留作準備。今年另有預期增加的51兆韓元稅收尚未分配。朴洪根反對立即將全部額外收入還債，因為日後稅收若減弱，可能被迫以更高利率重新借款。

## 債權保障與重整條款出現變化

歐洲收購融資文件開始納入AI衝擊，並改變債權人行使權利的條件。H.I.G. Capital為收購基礎設施服務商Terras Group多數股權所安排的€4.7億貸款，取得一項條款：若借款人認定受到AI影響，可延長違約寬限期。條款也涵蓋疫情、能源或資源價格急升、戰爭及恐怖主義。利息仍須支付，但只要公司認為AI影響仍在，債權人的救濟權利就可能暫停，且沒有明確終止日期。

這與未付息後通常30天的寬限期有重大差異，部分債權人反對，認為削弱基本償還保障。在貝恩資本收購福斯引擎業務Everllence控制權的等值€47億融資中，貸款人成功刪除類似措辭。因此，即使收購基金為預期表現良好的貸款爭取彈性，市場是否接受仍因交易而異。

面臨AI衝擊的客服外包商Konecta則已發生實際未付息事件。公司週一未支付利息，並取得足夠債權人暫緩追究，以繼續洽談削減超過€11億債務。參與債權人包括Benefit Street Partners、法國巴黎銀行、法國農業信貸銀行企業暨投資銀行、ICG Credit及景順。知情人士表示，日常營運未受影響。穆迪7月分析指出，過去三年平均每年自由現金流消耗近€1億，用於整合、近期則投入AI轉型計畫；預期未來一年現金流仍為負，之後才朝損益兩平方向改善。

軟體收購仍能融資，但成本不低。Bending Spoons行銷$10億5年期優先順位擔保美元債，殖利率指引位於10%區間低端，另有等值$5億歐元券，指引位於9%區間低端，預期評級為BB-。歐元券指引高於彭博泛歐高收益債指數的7.8%。持有AOL、Vimeo與Evernote等業務的該公司，其執行長Luca Ferrari將軟體估值下跌視為收購機會；擬議殖利率則反映投資人為這項策略提供資金所要求的補償。

Altice International約€80億債務重整，週二面臨談判保密協議期限。各方可延長協議，否則公司將公布原屬非公開的財務資訊。訴訟委員會持有的證券，先前因預期回收較高而享有價格溢價；部分參與者認為公開資訊將壓縮溢價，另一些則認為回收優勢仍在。Patrick Drahi與貸款人的補償，以及Elliott去年用來為超過€5億債務再融資的貸款如何處理，都尚未解決。貸款人也在紐約提告，指稱資產遭違法移轉至其無法追索之處。

美國另一項債權訴求則獲上訴法院支持。第二巡迴上訴法院維持PDVSA於2020年到期債券依委內瑞拉法律有效的判決，確認持有人有權由德拉瓦州出售Citgo母公司PDV Holding的程序中求償。債券以控制性股權為擔保，因而優先於其他求償人。Amber Energy得標方案中包含$20億支付這批債券，其$59億出價將使約$88億債權獲得清償並消滅。出售仍面臨另一項上訴，也尚未取得美國財政部海外資產控制辦公室授權；制裁同時阻止資產移轉及擔保品扣押。PDVSA仍可申請重審或尋求最高法院審查。

巴西方面，FS與Mubadala正探討在Raizen債務轉為股權前買入債權。FS聘請摩根士丹利，IG4則將興趣限縮至糖與乙醇部門相關債權，洽談仍在初步階段。Raizen重整涵蓋約650億巴西雷亞爾債務，依已議定的轉換安排，債權人將取得超過80%股權。潛在收購將改變重整過程中持有這些股權請求權的對象。

美國市政融資則有另一項再融資考驗。Quorum Health已取得轉為非營利機構所需的最後一項州政府批准，預期下月發行$13億債券，為約$9.7億企業債務再融資。美國銀行將承銷透過威斯康辛州機構發行的債券，架構上將由田納西州非營利機構QKA Health持有營運子公司。這家擁有11所醫院的集團可望取得免稅待遇、參與340B藥品定價計畫、接受可供抵稅的捐款，並可能獲得額外Medicaid給付。

交易經濟效益仍有爭議。Private Equity Stakeholder Project表示，交易會使長期債務增加30%，並讓投資人受益。QKA反駁，GoldenTree及其他債權人將減記債權，股東拿不到任何款項；以新債替換高成本短債後，年度利息費用將由2025會計年度$1.36億降至約$1.05億。高收益市政債能否成功發行仍是關鍵。Alvarez & Marsal的Jude Scaglione強調，在鄉村醫院經營艱困的環境中，須關注現金流、付款來源組合及債務負擔。

## 後續市場焦點

聯準會將於10月28日18:00 UTC公布決策，主席Kevin Warsh於18:30 UTC舉行記者會，市場共識為政策利率維持4%。信心回升與惠譽的通膨廣度研究，使本次會議面對更強的需求及通膨背景；看多美債部位增加，也提高市場對主席如何談論進一步緊縮的敏感度。渣打銀行Dan Pan以鷹派按兵不動為基本情境，但認為立即升息的風險可能遭低估。

週四美國數據將在政策決策之後，補上最新產出與通膨資訊。第三季GDP共識為3.2%，前期2.2%，亞特蘭大聯準銀行模型最新估計則為3.4%。9月核心PCE預期月增0.3%、年增3.1%，前期為0.2%及3%；整體PCE預期月增0.5%、年增3.6%。個人支出預期增加0.6%，前期0.9%，所得預期增加0.3%，前期0.2%。週五第三季僱用成本指數預期增加0.8%，前期0.9%。決策者發言之後，這些數據將更清楚呈現支出韌性與價格壓力廣度、持續性之間的關係。

加拿大週三決策面臨不同選擇。市場及加拿大最大幾家銀行的多數經濟學家預期升息至2.5%，將是逾三年來首次緊縮。核心通膨仍接近2%，能源向其他價格廣泛傳導的情況不多，但整體通膨維持約3%，家庭長期通膨預期升高，企業也愈來愈預期轉嫁成本。連續兩個月就業下降及房市低迷，則形成反向拉力。Macklem與資深副總裁Carolyn Rogers將於渥太華時間上午10:30發言，決策同時將公布新預測及央行Prima模型細節。

智利在美國收盤時公布一致決議，連續第七次會議維持利率4.5%，但警告通膨風險已顯著增加，目前經濟疲弱可能比預期更久。9月通膨為4.1%，受訪經濟學家估今年成長僅0.2%，2027年回升至3%。接下來須看燃料及匯率衝擊的持續性與傳導，央行原估2027年第二季通膨回到3%的路徑已受壓。豐業銀行預期12月15日升息25個基點，1月可能再升一次，其他分析師仍認為可能繼續按兵不動。

日本週五決策之前，已有兩項通膨加速數據。彭博調查中沒有經濟學家預期立即升息，超過80%則預期12月行動。因此，除利率決定外，日本央行是否正式判定基礎通膨已達2%目標，也相當重要。歐洲央行週四開會，面對信貸供需均走弱的新證據。法國週五公布通膨與GDP，預期年通膨3.6%、季成長僅0.1%，將直接檢視家庭情況惡化及融資壓力。

英國週三預算案將確立支出與借款安排，John Healey預計宣布全國生活工資提高約4%，18至20歲勞工的工資也將有類似百分比增幅。美國11月2日公布融資估計，接著是11月3日選舉及隔日季度再融資公告。分析師推測長天期標售可能縮減、國庫券發行增加，使融資年期組合成為有別於國會控制權所帶來財政影響的另一項曲線因素。

Alphabet、微軟及亞馬遜財報，將為重新升溫的AI融資需求提供下一輪營運比較。博通未來發債再融資仍取決於市況，更多銀行的承諾則將顯示其優先順位融資分散到多少機構。Stellantis週三公布財報，分析師預期第三季營收€364億，去年同期€372億，自由現金流為負€34億。其混合資本債至首次贖回日殖利率超過11%，發行時為6.875%。現金消耗及管理層展望是眼前信用焦點：德意志銀行認為財測仍可達成，巴克萊則認為可持續改善最快要到第四季。

以色列選舉及區域外交仍各自構成能源風險。選前民調顯示，兩大政治陣營均未確定能取得執政多數；伊朗的談判條件與華府核議題要求仍有落差。即使週二油價下跌，油價衝擊會持續多久仍未明朗。這將影響接下來的政策決定，因為同樣昂貴的燃料，一方面支持能源生產國所得，另一方面擠壓消費者，並加重其他地區融資負擔。

overall_summary.headline: 美國消費者信心回升，美債殖利率小幅走高、曲線趨平
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國10月消費者信心由修正後84.2回升至91.7，遠高於預期81，科技股也走高，美債則小幅下跌。2年期殖利率上升2.1個基點至4.7369%，10年期上升0.83個基點至4.9967%，2年與10年期利差收窄1.27個基點至25.98個基點。10年期實質殖利率與通膨補償同步增加，前者上升0.37個基點，損益兩平通膨率上升0.46個基點。當日小幅回落未明顯侵蝕近期長天期公債漲幅，主要支撐仍來自實質殖利率下降。

銀行正準備在2027年第一季透過投資等級債，為博通晶片融資方案中最高約$210億進行再融資，仍須視市況而定。出租予Anthropic的設備及博通明訂的殘值支持，是此結構的基礎。Meta另已完成$250億普通股與$125億特別股出售，展現股票融資需求，帶動半導體股上漲3.60%。

布蘭特原油下跌1.61%至$113.95，但惠譽發現，美國9月CPI組成項目中，46%的年漲幅超過3%。法國消費者信心降至13年低點，10年期法債相對德債利差擴大7個基點至161個基點。聯準會面對更強的家庭部門訊號及持續廣泛的通膨壓力，美債多頭部位增加，也使市場對意外偏鷹的訊息更敏感。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries edged lower as a stronger U.S. consumer-confidence reading and another advance in technology shares met a market already leaning toward a Federal Reserve pause followed by renewed tightening. The two-year yield rose 2.1 basis points to 4.7369%, while the 10-year increased just 0.83 basis point to 4.9967%. Longer maturities again held up better than the front end, extending the curve's flattening rather than reversing the recent recovery in government bonds.

The day's larger financing development came from artificial intelligence. Banks are preparing to refinance as much as about $21 billion of Broadcom's chip-financing package in the investment-grade bond market early next year. The proposed issuance, backed by equipment leased to Anthropic and a specified Broadcom residual-value commitment, gives creditors a clearer view of both the prospective supply and the protection behind it. Meta's completed common and preferred share sales supplied a separate demonstration of capital availability, helping semiconductor shares rise 3.60% even as investors continued to distinguish between borrowers and financing structures.

Falling oil offered some relief ahead of the Fed decision, with Brent down 1.61% to $113.95 a barrel, but fresh inflation research pointed beyond energy: Fitch found that 46% of U.S. CPI components had annual increases above 3% in September. France meanwhile surrendered part of its rating-relief rally as consumer confidence reached a 13-year low. The result was a quiet U.S. government-bond session alongside consequential changes in the terms of corporate funding and the distribution of sovereign risk.

## Confidence Rebounds as the Treasury Curve Flattens

Tuesday's Treasury losses were modest and concentrated in maturities more sensitive to the next policy decisions. The five-year yield increased 1.79 basis points to 4.8441%, while the 30-year rose 0.75 basis point to 5.3103%. The 2s10s spread narrowed 1.27 basis points to 25.98 basis points, and the two- to 30-year gap contracted 1.35 basis points to 57.34 basis points. The front end's weaker performance accompanied a significant upside surprise in household confidence, without a wholesale reassessment of longer-term yields.

The weekly comparison still favored longer debt. Ten-year yields were 11.18 basis points lower than a week earlier and 16.63 basis points lower over the month, against declines of 3.92 and 11.71 basis points at two years. At 30 years, yields were down 10.95 basis points over the week and 18.37 basis points over the month. Tuesday gave back only a small part of that decline.

Both real yields and inflation compensation contributed to the small 10-year increase. The TIPS real yield rose 0.37 basis point to 2.6416%, while the breakeven increased 0.46 basis point to 2.3551%. Over the week, real yields had fallen 10.87 basis points and breakevens only 0.31 basis point. The monthly comparison was more striking: a decline of 18.24 basis points in real yields alongside a 1.61-basis-point increase in inflation compensation. The sustained support for nominal Treasuries therefore continued to come predominantly through lower real yields, rather than a broad retreat in expected inflation.

Conference Board consumer confidence rose to 91.7 in October from a revised 84.2, decisively exceeding the 81 consensus. Bloomberg described the first increase in four months as reflecting brighter assessments of labor-market and business conditions, with the result above every forecast in its economist survey. That rebound gave the Fed a materially stronger household signal on the eve of its meeting.

Business investment readings were less uniformly strong. September durable-goods orders increased 1.8%, above the 1.5% consensus and a revised 0.1% gain in August. Orders excluding transportation rose 0.5%, accelerating from 0.3% but falling short of the expected 0.6%. Non-defense orders excluding aircraft also increased 0.5%, below the 0.7% consensus and slower than the previous 1.6%. Orders excluding defense rose 2.2% after a revised 0.3%. The headline acceleration thus came with a more moderate result in the separately measured non-defense, ex-aircraft category.

Weekly ADP employment increased 16,800, compared with a revised 17,500 previously. Regional business surveys offered a mixed but generally firmer services picture. Richmond's October manufacturing index remained at minus 2 rather than reaching the expected zero, although its shipments index improved to zero from minus 5. Richmond services revenues rose to 2 from zero. The Dallas Fed services index increased to 4.0 from minus 1.8, and its services revenues measure advanced to 4.4 from minus 0.9. These were distinct improvements in reported regional service activity alongside continued softness in the Richmond manufacturing headline.

Housing remained constrained by financing costs. September new-home sales fell 0.6% to an annualized 676,000 from a revised 680,000, following a revised 5.1% monthly increase. The level exceeded the 650,000 calendar consensus; Bloomberg's separate economist survey had looked for 651,000. The median sale price declined 3.9% from a year earlier to $400,400, the seventh annual decline in the first nine months of 2026. Nationwide economist Daniel Vielhaber attributed the maintenance of sales more to builder price concessions and mortgage incentives than to strong underlying demand.

The regional detail reinforced that restraint. Sales in the South, the largest market, dropped 6.6% to an annualized 413,000, and the Midwest also weakened, offsetting gains in the West and Northeast. Inventory fell 2.3% from a year earlier to 476,000 homes, equivalent to 8.4 months of sales. That was the lowest months-of-supply reading this year but still well above pre-pandemic levels. The monthly sales estimate was also imprecise: the government's 90% confidence interval ran from a 14.4% decline to a 13.2% increase.

Other housing releases showed the difference between current financing pressure and lagged price measures. Final September building permits fell 0.4% to 1.398 million, against expectations for a 0.2% decline and a 1.4 million level. August's S&P/Case-Shiller annual home-price increase accelerated to 2.7% from 2.5%, exceeding the 2.5% consensus, while its monthly measure fell 0.4% after no change. The separately titled House Price Index rose 0.3% on the month, above the 0.2% consensus and revised prior gain, but annual growth slowed to 2.4% from a revised 2.5%.

The Atlanta Fed's GDPNow estimate for Q3 slipped to 3.4% from 3.5%. That model update accompanied a 9.3% annual increase in Redbook sales for the week ended October 24, up from 9%, leaving the activity picture stronger in some household measures than in housing. Treasury's five-year auction cleared at 4.845%, compared with 5.033% at the preceding sale.

Inflation breadth provided an independent counterweight to the decline in oil. Fitch's new cross-country assessment put the share of U.S. CPI components rising more than 3% annually at 46% in September, twice the 23% average in 2018-2019. The corresponding shares were 36% in the euro area, 41% in Japan and 42% in Britain. Fitch's Olu Sonola said U.S. breadth had begun increasing before the latest acceleration in headline inflation, suggesting that wider price pressure could delay convergence to target even if energy eased.

Brent's decline came as traders assessed regional diplomacy and the Israeli election, while WTI fell 1.85% to $99.88. Iran reiterated demands for an end to the U.S. naval blockade and sanctions as conditions for peace talks, while Washington sought nuclear concessions. The daily decline left Brent 16.94% above its month-earlier level. Stocks responded more decisively to improving sentiment: the S&P 500 gained 0.60% to 7,722.60 and the Nasdaq 100 rose 1.29%, while the Dollar Index increased 0.40% to 102.365. High-yield fund HYG returned about 0.52% and investment-grade fund LQD about 0.27%.

Positioning raised the stakes of the next Fed communication. JPMorgan's survey for the week to October 26 showed outright long positions increasing 6 percentage points, with neutral positions down 4 points and shorts down 2. Net longs reached their highest since September 8. Citigroup's David Bieber described a tactical move into long Treasury and European-bond positions within a market that remained structurally short. Swaps in Bloomberg's Tuesday account assigned roughly an 8% chance to an October increase and more than 90% to a December move, leaving a hawkish surprise capable of challenging the recent accumulation of bullish exposure.

## AI Financing Opens a Large New Bond Pipeline

Broadcom's $63 billion financing for chips destined for Anthropic now has a more explicit route into public credit markets. Bank of America, Citigroup and Morgan Stanley helped arrange the package, and other banks were expected to submit commitments in the coming days. Banks are lending about $42 billion, as much as half of which could be refinanced through U.S. investment-grade bonds in Q1 2027, people familiar with the transaction told Bloomberg.

The structure borrows through a special-purpose company to acquire equipment, including chips for data centers, and leases it to Anthropic. Lease payments service the borrowing. The $42 billion bank-funded portion is senior secured, giving lenders first claim on the vehicle's assets, and Broadcom supplies residual-value support. Its filing defines potential liability as the difference between 72.5% of outstanding lease amounts and the value of the AI racks received upon an asset sale. Broadcom considers a liability under that backstop unlikely.

That specified support is central to the proposed financing, rather than an unlimited guarantee of the whole package. The eventual bonds would probably mature in around five years and repay principal over their lives. Their final size and issuance timing remain dependent on market conditions. Blackstone is anchoring the rest of the financing with a $9 billion commitment.

The prospective $21 billion public sale would bring a sizeable portion of a bank-underwritten equipment transaction into the same market already absorbing extraordinary technology borrowing. Bloomberg put AI-related borrowing across markets globally above $455 billion this year. Within the narrower global high-grade market, funding had exceeded $300 billion, roughly triple last year's amount. These totals describe different financing universes, but both establish the scale against which the next transactions will compete for investor capital.

Meta supplied new evidence of equity demand rather than another proposed bond issue. It sold $25 billion of common shares and $12.5 billion of preferred shares and said it planned to raise as much as $60 billion more for AI spending. Its total capital-raising ambition had increased to almost $98 billion. The common-share sale was five times oversubscribed, helping the technology recovery extend even as the financing calendar grew.

BlackRock fixed-income chief Rick Rieder argued that the new supply was improving the compensation available to creditors. He said he had spent the weekend examining and participating substantially in transactions, favoring secured debt from established companies and cash-generating assets. In his assessment, short-dated, single-A-rated portfolios could earn about 7%, an attractive alternative to taking longer Treasury duration.

Existing bonds showed how much pricing had changed. Meta's 2036 debt traded more than 130 basis points over Treasuries, against 90 basis points at its April sale. A Bloomberg index put U.S. investment-grade yields at 5.9%, after almost 6.1% earlier this month. Rieder regarded recent hyperscaler pricing as more reasonable given the large funding requirement. Citadel co-chief investment officer Pablo Salame supplied the opposing concern: extraordinary capital demand was meeting lenders unwilling to assume all the risk, leaving room for casualties.

The disagreement over government bonds was equally clear. JPMorgan Asset Management's Bob Michele forecast U.S. bond returns of about 7%-8% over the next 12 months, combining carry with expected price appreciation. He saw the most value at the long end and argued that a hawkish December Fed message could support those maturities by demonstrating vigilance on inflation and growth. Rieder instead described the 10-year Treasury as increasingly a market barometer rather than the core opportunity in fixed income. Neither view required Tuesday's small yield change to settle the competition between sovereign duration and corporate income.

BCE's asset sale offered another example of how AI spending can compete with deleveraging. Quebec pension manager La Caisse agreed to pay C$2.45 billion for 49.9% of the telecom company's wireless towers. The resulting TowerCo would have more than 5,000 sites. BCE described the transaction as consistent with strengthening its balance sheet and investing in growth, while Scotiabank analyst Maher Yaghi expected the proceeds to be recycled into AI services rather than materially reducing leverage. He judged the transaction cash-negative in the short term until new AI investments contributed. BCE targets net debt of 3.5 times adjusted EBITDA by the end of 2027, compared with about 3.8 times at last year's end.

Market structure is also changing beneath the issuance boom. In research dated Tuesday, Barclays strategist Zornitsa Todorova found that an issuer's three most-traded U.S. bonds accounted for about 35% of its securities' trading volume, down 5 percentage points from January 2023. European credit had seen a similar decline over roughly three and a half years. The broadening came mainly in investment grade; high-yield and hyperscaler trading remained more concentrated. Todorova argued that more activity across an issuer's curve could reduce the valuation gap between benchmark and less frequently traded bonds, giving investors more maturity choices as supply expands.

## France's Reversal Sharpens the Fiscal Divide

French bonds lost part of their rating-relief gains as a fresh confidence shock exposed the economic costs of the country's political and financing strains. The 10-year spread over Germany widened 7 basis points to 161 basis points, reversing some of the previous session's 14-basis-point narrowing. Insee's October consumer-confidence gauge fell 5 points to 80, below the 85 median forecast and every estimate in Bloomberg's survey, reaching its lowest in 13 years.

Households' assessment of past living standards was the weakest since measurement began in 1972. Unemployment expectations reached their highest since the pandemic, and the outlook for personal finances was the worst in four years. Expected inflation also increased. Much of the interviewing preceded the most severe unrest: the survey ended October 19, but most responses were collected early in its three-week period, before the October 17 violence. The new figures therefore show substantial household deterioration without capturing the full subsequent disruption.

The financing exposure runs through both the investor base and the banking system. Central-bank filings show non-residents owning about 60% of French debt, near a decade high, compared with about 31% in the U.S. at the end of 2025 and 34% in Britain at the end of June. French insurers and banks held 9.2% and 10.5%, respectively, at the end of Q2. UniCredit's Luca Cazzulani identified the remaining scope for foreign selling as a vulnerability, while Pimco's Konstantin Veit said authorities could encourage domestic bank purchases if demand at regular auctions became problematic.

BNP Paribas, Societe Generale and Credit Agricole together held roughly EUR54 billion of French sovereign debt, rising to about EUR104 billion including insurance operations, according to Bloomberg Intelligence. Much of the additional insurance exposure lies with policyholders. BI analyst Philip Richards regarded concerns about the banks' direct sovereign risk as excessive given amortized-cost accounting and potential hedges. Their Q2 CET1 ratios were 13.0%, 13.2% and 11.3%, respectively, comfortably above regulatory minima.

The more diffuse threat is weaker activity, reduced loan demand and losses on holdings marked to market. The ECB's new Bank Lending Survey showed euro-area banks tightening credit standards in Q3 while loan demand waned. Higher perceived risk and lower risk tolerance drove the supply restraint; the general level of interest rates was the main drag on demand, with weaker small-business fixed investment and alternative financing also contributing. Banks reported a mildly negative effect on financing conditions and liquidity from the ECB's shrinking portfolio, alongside a slightly positive profitability effect as higher net interest income outweighed small capital losses.

That survey gives the ECB a new reason for caution as it weighs inflation against financing restraint. It also found gradual, sustained growth in demand for AI infrastructure loans. Most banks had not established quantitative criteria specifically for AI-related lending, though a small number were incorporating adoption and associated risks into qualitative borrower assessments. Credit demand was weakening overall while one capital-intensive sector continued to require more funding.

Fresh fiscal analysis questioned whether the U.S. could obtain lasting bond-market relief simply from divided government. TD Securities strategists Molly Brooks and Gennadiy Goldberg projected that even a gridlock outcome would leave the deficit rising to 6.4% of GDP in fiscal 2027 from 5.9%, because substantive spending changes were unlikely. Diamond Hill's Henry Song argued that stabilizing debt now required policy action, not merely avoiding new legislation, with public debt above $32 trillion and annual net interest costs exceeding $1 trillion.

MUFG's George Goncalves offered a different conditional route to lower yields: a Democratic wave could bring tighter AI regulation, weakening equities and growth while reducing related debt issuance. SMBC's Joseph Abate instead saw a possibility that larger Democratic gains would push Republicans toward affordability measures and additional spending. The disagreement concerned the policy consequences of the election, rather than an automatic Treasury benefit from legislative paralysis.

The fiscal starting points also differ across countries. In a comparison published Tuesday, Bloomberg's Chris Anstey highlighted IMF estimates putting French government revenue above 50% of GDP this year, against under 30% in the U.S. France's already large tax burden limits the scope for raising more revenue without economic damage; Washington has more economic room to do so, although the political appetite remains weak. For French borrowers, that narrower adjustment space sits beside the new fall in confidence and renewed spread widening.

## Asian Funding Access Diverges

Indonesia's sovereign and corporate markets supplied fresh evidence that the governance-driven equity shock was affecting financing beyond stocks. The 10-year government yield rose 5 basis points to 7.54%, its highest since October 2022, while the rupiah moved within 0.2% of its record low. Demand at Tuesday's government auction fell to a three-year low: bids of 31.1 trillion rupiah only slightly exceeded the 30 trillion-rupiah target, and the government sold 20.7 trillion rupiah.

Foreign participation offered a counterweight. Overseas holdings of sovereign debt had increased $509 million this month, suggesting some investors were responding to higher yields. Mandiri Sekuritas researcher Handy Yunianto saw the principal risk from MSCI's warning as continued equity outflows pressuring the rupiah, rather than a direct index effect on bonds. He put the 10-year fair-value range at 7.5%-7.7% and expected scope for yields to decline if risk aversion and oil prices eased. High oil also enlarges the subsidy bill, adding a fiscal channel to the currency pressure.

Bank KB Indonesia postponed the dollar-bond sale it had begun marketing Monday, citing volatility. The planned three-year note carried an expected BBB rating from Fitch and initial guidance around 275 basis points over Treasuries, compared with about 120 basis points on similarly rated Asian corporate debt. Kookmin Bank owns two-thirds of the lender. Nomura's Nicholas Yap linked the difficulty partly to Indonesia's broader sentiment deterioration but also to the bank's small size, weak standalone fundamentals and effort to issue before month-end. He expected government-owned borrowers with sound fundamentals to retain access, albeit at larger new-issue premiums.

Samsung Life demonstrated the distinction. Its debut dollar subordinated sale raised $1.5 billion Monday with a 6.875% coupon, below initial thoughts around 7%, according to details reported Tuesday. The amount was a record for a Korean life insurer, and the notes had expected ratings of A+ from Fitch and A2 from Moody's. Nearly half the participants were global investors, including U.S. and European buyers. Proceeds support capital adequacy, shareholder returns and new growth activities. Fitch's Sue Kim attributed the result partly to selective demand for stronger issuers and Samsung Life's limited capital sensitivity to market movements.

China's government and corporate debt moved further apart. The PBOC injected a net 1.01 trillion yuan through reverse repos, the largest daily net addition in Bloomberg's records, and the five-year sovereign yield briefly touched 1.34%, close to a record closing low in Chinabond data extending to 2002. Huafa's offshore yuan debt, by contrast, suffered another sharp adjustment: one bond was indicated down a record 17% Tuesday to about 74% of face value. That price deterioration was the new development after its missed trust-product payments and bank-extension requests had become known. RatingDog's Yao Yu continued to expect strong local-government support, while Bloomberg Intelligence's Andrew Chan emphasized weaker refinancing support for locally backed developers than for central-government enterprises.

Japan received two separate inflation signals. September corporate services prices rose 3.7% annually, accelerating from a revised 3.5%; ocean freight costs surged 97.7%, the largest increase in data back to 1986. Separately, the BOJ's consumer-price measure excluding fresh food and special factors rose 3.2% from 2.6%, its highest in three years. The special-factor adjustment includes gasoline and utility subsidies, making that measure distinct from the government's consumer-price series excluding fresh food. Both releases strengthened the case for continued normalization after September's increase to a 1.25% policy rate.

Higher yields were also changing insurer allocation. Second-half plans from 10 major Japanese life insurers showed widespread replacement of low-yielding bonds with higher-yielding securities, even where redemptions left total domestic holdings flat or lower. Nippon Life expected holdings to decline while conducting such switches, but described current rates as attractive. Other firms were shifting from currency-hedged foreign bonds into domestic debt. Okasan Securities' Naoya Hasegawa expected stronger demand around 3% for 10-year JGBs and 4% for 30-year bonds on a simple-yield basis. Those are prospective buying levels, rather than Tuesday market quotations.

South Korea identified a different buffer against funding pressure. Budget Minister Park Hong Keun said the planned Future Response Fund could be used to reduce issuance further if yields surged or conditions deteriorated. The existing plan cuts next year's debt issuance by 12.5 trillion won, with net issuance of 96.3 trillion won and gross sales around 223 trillion won. The fund is expected to receive 162.3 trillion won next year, with roughly two-thirds remaining in reserves after policy spending and issuance reductions. Another 51 trillion won of expected extra tax revenue this year remains unallocated. Park argued against using the entire windfall immediately for debt repayment, since weaker later revenue could force renewed borrowing at higher rates.

## Creditor Protections and Restructuring Terms Change

European buyout documentation is beginning to recognize AI disruption in a way that changes enforcement rights. H.I.G. Capital secured language in the EUR470 million loan backing its majority purchase of infrastructure-services company Terras Group that can extend default grace periods when the borrower determines it is affected by AI. The clause also covers pandemics, sharp energy or resource-price increases, war and terrorism. Interest remains owed, but creditor remedies can be suspended for as long as the company feels the AI impact, which has no clear end date.

That is a material departure from the usual grace period, typically 30 days after a missed interest payment. Some creditors objected that the wording undermined basic repayment protection. Lenders successfully removed similar language from Bain Capital's EUR4.7 billion-equivalent financing for its controlling stake in Volkswagen's engine business Everllence. Acceptance therefore remains transaction-specific, even as sponsors seek flexibility in loans they expect to perform well.

Konecta provided an actual payment event in an AI-exposed business. The customer-service outsourcer skipped an interest payment Monday and obtained temporary forbearance from enough creditors to continue negotiating a reduction of more than EUR1.1 billion of debt. The group includes Benefit Street Partners, BNP Paribas, Credit Agricole CIB, ICG Credit and Invesco. Day-to-day operations were unaffected, according to a person familiar with the discussions. Moody's July analysis put average annual free-cash-flow consumption near EUR100 million over the past three years, financing integration and more recently an AI transformation plan; it expected cash flow to remain negative over the next year before moving toward break-even.

Software acquisition financing nevertheless remained available at a price. Bending Spoons marketed $1 billion of five-year senior secured dollar notes in the low 10% area and a $500 million-equivalent euro tranche in the low 9% area, with expected BB- ratings. The euro indication exceeded the 7.8% yield on the Bloomberg Pan-European High Yield Index. Chief Executive Luca Ferrari regarded falling software valuations as acquisition opportunities for the owner of businesses including AOL, Vimeo and Evernote, while the proposed yields showed the compensation sought to fund that strategy.

Altice International's roughly EUR8 billion overhaul approached a Tuesday deadline for its negotiating confidentiality agreement. The parties could extend it; otherwise the company would publish previously private financial information. Securities held by the litigation committee had traded at a premium on expectations of stronger recoveries. Some participants expected disclosure to compress that premium, while others thought the recovery advantage would persist. Compensation for Patrick Drahi and lenders remained unresolved, as did treatment of an Elliott loan used last year to refinance more than EUR500 million. Those negotiations sit alongside lenders' New York lawsuit alleging that assets were unlawfully moved beyond their reach.

A U.S. appeals ruling advanced a different creditor claim. The Second Circuit upheld the validity under Venezuelan law of PDVSA bonds due in 2020, affirming holders' rights to seek payment from the Delaware sale of Citgo parent PDV Holding. The bonds' controlling-stake collateral gives them priority over other claimants. Amber Energy's winning proposal includes $2 billion to pay the notes; its $5.9 billion bid would extinguish about $8.8 billion of claims. The sale remains subject to a separate appeal and lacks OFAC authorization, with sanctions preventing both the property transfer and seizure of collateral. PDVSA can seek rehearing or Supreme Court review.

In Brazil, FS and Mubadala were exploring purchases of Raizen debt ahead of its conversion into equity. FS hired Morgan Stanley, while IG4 narrowed its interest to credit associated with the sugar and ethanol division. The talks are preliminary. Raizen's restructuring covers about 65 billion reais of debt, with agreed conversions set to give creditors more than 80% of its capital. The prospective purchases would change who holds those ownership claims as the restructuring proceeds.

U.S. municipal finance offered a separate refinancing test. Quorum Health obtained the final state approval needed for a planned nonprofit conversion and expects a $1.3 billion bond sale next month, refinancing about $970 million of corporate debt. Bank of America would underwrite bonds issued through a Wisconsin agency, placing Tennessee nonprofit QKA Health above the operating subsidiaries. The 11-hospital chain could gain tax exemptions, access to the 340B drug-pricing program, deductible donations and potentially supplemental Medicaid payments.

The economics remain disputed. The Private Equity Stakeholder Project said the transaction would increase long-term debt 30% and benefit investors. QKA countered that GoldenTree and other debt holders would take haircuts, equity holders would receive nothing, and annual interest expense would decline to about $105 million from $136 million in fiscal 2025 as high-cost short-term debt was replaced. Successful high-yield municipal placement is still essential. Alvarez & Marsal's Jude Scaglione emphasized cash flow, payer mix and debt load in a difficult rural-hospital environment.

## Forward Market Significance

The Fed decision on October 28 is due at 18:00 UTC, followed by Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference at 18:30 UTC. Consensus expects the policy rate to remain at 4%. The new confidence rebound and Fitch's breadth findings give the meeting a firmer demand and inflation backdrop, while bullish positioning increases sensitivity to the chair's treatment of further tightening. Standard Chartered's Dan Pan regarded a hawkish hold as the baseline but thought the risk of an immediate increase might be underestimated.

Thursday's U.S. releases will put new output and inflation observations beside that decision. Q3 GDP consensus is 3.2%, compared with 2.2% previously and the Atlanta Fed model's latest 3.4% estimate. September core PCE is expected to rise 0.3% monthly and 3.1% annually, against 0.2% and 3%; headline expectations are 0.5% and 3.6%. Personal spending consensus is a 0.6% increase after 0.9%, with income expected up 0.3% after 0.2%. Friday's Employment Cost Index is expected to rise 0.8% in Q3 after 0.9%. The sequence will sharpen the comparison between resilient spending and the breadth and persistence of price pressure after policymakers have spoken.

Canada's Wednesday decision presents a different immediate choice. Markets and most economists at the largest Canadian banks expect an increase to 2.5%, the first tightening in more than three years. Core inflation remains near 2% and broad energy pass-through has been scant, but headline inflation has stayed around 3%, longer-term household expectations have risen and companies increasingly expect to pass on costs. Two consecutive months of employment losses and subdued housing pull the other way. Macklem and Senior Deputy Governor Carolyn Rogers speak at 10:30 a.m. Ottawa time, with new forecasts and details of the bank's Prima model accompanying the decision.

Chile held at 4.5% for a seventh consecutive meeting in a unanimous decision announced at the U.S. close, while warning that inflation risks had increased considerably and that current economic weakness could last longer than expected. September inflation was 4.1%; surveyed economists see only 0.2% growth this year before 3% in 2027. The next assessment turns on the persistence and pass-through of fuel and currency shocks, with the bank's projected return to 3% inflation in Q2 2027 under pressure. Scotiabank expects a quarter-point increase December 15 and possibly another in January, while other analysts still allow for a further hold.

Japan's Friday decision follows the two fresh inflation accelerations. No economist in Bloomberg's survey expected an immediate increase, while more than 80% expected a December move. Whether the BOJ formally judges underlying inflation to have reached its 2% objective will therefore matter alongside the rate decision. The ECB meets Thursday with new evidence that both credit supply and demand are weakening. France's Friday inflation and GDP releases are expected to show 3.6% annual inflation and only 0.1% quarterly growth, adding a direct test of the household deterioration and financing strain.

Britain's Wednesday budget will set spending and borrowing terms while John Healey is expected to announce an approximately 4% increase in the national living wage, with a similar percentage rise for workers aged 18-20. In the U.S., November 2 financing estimates precede the November 3 election and the following day's quarterly refunding announcement. Analysts' speculation about smaller long-maturity auctions and more bill issuance makes the funding mix a separate prospective curve influence from the fiscal effects of congressional control.

Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon earnings will provide the next operating comparison for the renewed appetite to finance AI. Broadcom's prospective bond takeout depends on market conditions, and additional banks' commitments will establish how widely its senior financing is distributed. Stellantis reports Wednesday with analysts forecasting EUR36.4 billion of Q3 revenue against EUR37.2 billion a year earlier and EUR3.4 billion of negative free cash flow. Its hybrids yield more than 11% to first call, compared with 6.875% at issuance. Cash burn and management's outlook are the immediate credit questions: Deutsche Bank expects guidance to remain achievable, while Barclays sees sustainable improvement no earlier than Q4.

Israel's election and regional diplomacy remain independent energy risks. Neither main political bloc was assured a governing majority in pre-vote polling. Iran's conditions for talks and Washington's nuclear demands remain apart, leaving the duration of the oil shock unresolved even after Tuesday's price decline. That duration matters across the forthcoming policy decisions because the same expensive fuel is supporting income in energy-producing economies while squeezing consumers and widening the financing burden elsewhere.

overall_summary.headline: Treasury yields edge higher and the curve flattens as U.S. consumer confidence rebounds
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries edged lower as October consumer confidence rebounded to 91.7 from a revised 84.2, well above the 81 consensus, and technology shares advanced. The 2-year yield rose 2.1 basis points to 4.7369%, while the 10-year increased 0.83 basis point to 4.9967%. The 2s10s spread narrowed 1.27 basis points to 25.98 basis points. Both real yields and inflation compensation contributed: the 10-year real yield rose 0.37 basis point and the breakeven increased 0.46 basis point. The day's small reversal left the recent longer-maturity rally largely intact, with its support still predominantly coming from lower real yields.

Banks are preparing to refinance as much as about $21 billion of Broadcom's chip-financing package through investment-grade bonds in Q1 2027, subject to market conditions. Equipment leased to Anthropic and specified Broadcom residual-value support underpin the structure. Meta's completed $25 billion common-share and $12.5 billion preferred-share sales separately demonstrated equity funding demand, helping semiconductor shares advance 3.60%.

Brent fell 1.61% to $113.95, but Fitch found that 46% of U.S. CPI components were rising more than 3% annually in September. France's 10-year spread over Germany widened 7 basis points to 161 basis points as consumer confidence hit a 13-year low. The Fed now faces a firmer household signal and persistent inflation breadth, with increased Treasury long positioning raising sensitivity to a hawkish surprise.
overall_summary.summary: Longer maturities held up better ahead of the Fed decision, while Broadcom's prospective bond financing for Anthropic equipment brought a large new supply pipeline into focus and falling oil left broader inflation pressure unresolved.
